ADMIT dsh 0.2.2-rc.5 AS A MEASURED HANDS RELEASE, WITH ITS OWN COMPOSED SET (the operator, 2026-11-19: "can we update dsh to latest and qualify it for review seats?").

This unit is the first step only: npm's `latest` and `next` are 0.2.2-rc.5 (published 2026-11-18). Today Brokkr refuses it for every hands seat, because `Release::named` admits only the measured 0.2.1-rc.2, 0.2.1-rc.3 and 0.2.2-rc.1. The review-seat qualification follows in later units, and is NOT this one's.

Read first:
- docs/evidence/adapters/dsh-hands-0-2-2.md, all of it, especially "Re-measuring a new dsh release";
- PR #1056, which admitted 0.2.2-rc.1. Its files are this unit's files and nothing more: crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters/dsh_hands.rs, dsh_hands/composition.rs, dsh_hands/tests.rs, and the evidence record;
- `MEASURED_VERSIONS`, `Release`, `Release::versions`, `Release::named`, `V0_2_2_PINNED`, `judge` and `hands_rows`.

Verify every name against the tree, not this list.

The branch is story-dsh0225-measured-release, checked out in this worktree off origin/main at 1c2e29fc. When you are done, the branch is 1c2e29fc plus your commits. Do not rebase, squash, amend or merge main: the controller restacks. Where a choice is left open below, implement the option marked recommended, keep it small, and say which you took in your notes.

THE MEASUREMENT (the controller's, 2026-11-19, Linux workstation, by the record's procedure). This seat has no dsh and no network: every live figure below is the controller's, and the record says so in its Provenance table.
- **Install:** `npm install --prefix /var/tmp/dsh-0.2.2-rc.5 @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.2-rc.5`, 673 packages. `dsh --version` = 0.2.2-rc.5. The installed 0.2.1-rc.2 and the operator's ~/.dsh were untouched.
- **Home:** a scratch `DSH_HOME` (/var/tmp/dsh-home-0225) holding a copy of the operator's `headless` profile, identical to the one 0.2.2-rc.1 was measured with. The copy's `node_modules` held 0 entries, so every row is 0.2.2-rc.5's own.
- **Step 3, `dsh --profile headless --dump-config` (no model call):** 101 top-level rows against 0.2.2-rc.1's 99. Every other (id, name) pair is unchanged. The deltas, by (id, name):
  - added `agent-team` = `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-team` (config `maxTasks: 256`, enabled by default);
  - added `tool-agent-team` = `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-agent-team` (no config, enabled by default);
  - changed `deepseek-account`: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-deepseek-account-platform` → `@deepseek-ai/dsh-deepseek-account` (still `disabled: true`).
  - The dump's sha256 starts 271ed858f3d14686.
- **Step 4, tool lists (one session each, `spark-glm/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3`):**
  - With the overlay's `agent-default-model` row alone: 24 tools.
  - With the 0.2.2 hands rows (the ten common rows plus the `tool-executor-ptc` pin): 8 tools: create_goal, get_goal, list_agents, send_message, todo_write, update_goal, wait_agent, working_directory.
  - Against 0.2.2-rc.1, both lists changed the same way: `interrupt_agent` is gone and `wait_agent` is new.
  - No team tool appears in either list.
- **Step 5:**
  - The six sandbox rows (`sandbox`, `sandbox-policy`, `bash-sandbox`, `pwsh-sandbox`, `permission`, `fs-sandbox`) keep their ids and package names.
  - `tool-executor-ptc` is `disabled: true` by default; `tool-executor-native` is enabled.
  - With the hands rows the dump still has 101 rows. The hands dump's sha256 starts be8e3716a26ffbf0.

THE CONTROLLER'S RULINGS (2026-11-19, under the operator's instruction and the standing ruling of 2026-11-04):
- **R1: its own release.** 0.2.2-rc.5 is a measured release with its own composed set. Recommended: a third `Release` (for example `V0_2_2_RC5`).
  - Its judge admits 0.2.2-rc.1's set, plus `agent-team` and `tool-agent-team`, with `deepseek-account` under its new package name, plus `brokkr-hands`: 102 rows in a seat's tree.
  - A row from another release's set is refused `Unmeasured`, naming the release, as #1056's judges do.
  - `Release::named` matches `0.2.2-rc.5` whole. 0.2.2-rc.2, rc.3 and rc.4 stay unmeasured and refuse, naming every measured release.
- **R2: fail closed on the new surface.** On 0.2.2-rc.5 the hands overlay writes `tool-agent-team` `disabled: true`, beside the ten common rows and the `tool-executor-ptc` pin.
  - A composed tree that enables `tool-agent-team` is refused `Composition::Enabled`.
  - `agent-team`, the host row with no tool, stays as composed. Say in the record why: it adds no tool to either list.
- **R3: 0.2.1 and 0.2.2-rc.1 are unchanged:** their overlay bytes, sets and refusal texts.
- **R4: the record.** Add a section to docs/evidence/adapters/dsh-hands-0-2-2.md, or a sibling record linked from it: provenance, install, the composition diff, both tool lists, the sandbox rows, and the two digests. Keep the "Pending" list true, and move nothing into it that this unit closes.
- **R5: carry #1056's lows only if they are in your way.** F1 is the direct assertion that the ten rows are disabled; F2 is the two homes of the disabled rows. Otherwise leave them, and say so.

TESTS (each named, each failing before your change):
- `judge` on an rc.5 fixture tree admits it;
- the same tree reported as 0.2.2-rc.1 refuses the two team rows `Unmeasured`;
- an rc.5 tree with `tool-agent-team` enabled refuses `Composition::Enabled`;
- `Release::named("0.2.2-rc.4")` and `("0.2.2")` refuse;
- the rc.5 hands overlay's bytes are pinned.

Removal controls (record each in the commit message, restored after the observed failure):
- (i) drop the `tool-agent-team` pin: the enabled-tree test fails;
- (ii) admit rc.5 into 0.2.2-rc.1's judge: the cross-release test fails.

THE JOURNAL RULE. Main is queue storage v6 or later. A brokkr built from this tree migrates any journal it opens for writing, and the lanes' pinned engines cannot read a migrated journal. Never run a brokkr built from this tree against a journal outside a test's own temporary directory.

THE EXACT COVERAGE GATE counts every line, branch and function of production code at 100%, closures included; test files are excluded. Give each new arm a test.

PUBLIC API: no change expected; say so.

GATES:
- cargo fmt --all -- --check
- cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
- cargo test -p brokkr-protocol --lib --locked -- --test-threads=16 adapters::dsh_hands (timeout 280)
- cargo test -p brokkr-protocol --lib --locked -- --test-threads=16 adapters:: (timeout 280)
- typos --hidden; quality/ratchet.sh files, clones, api and crap; git diff --check
- **TMPDIR** stays OUTSIDE this worktree (use /var/tmp, created in the same command if missing). Before reporting, `git status --short` shows no untracked file.
- **Foreground only.** Run every command in the foreground and wait for it. Never end your turn with a background job pending.
- **The workspace tool.** A seat whose commands run through the `workspace` tool has a 300-second response limit per call. Wrap every command in `timeout 280` there. A gate that still cannot finish is reported UNVERIFIED, not retried. Write your result file before any optional extra check.

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.


result.notes:
Admitted dsh 0.2.2-rc.5 as a third measured Release in one commit, 9f6e8e2d on 1c2e29fc. No rebase, squash or amend.

What changed:
- R1: a third Release, V0_2_2Rc5, the recommended option. Its version const is V0_2_2_RC_5. Release::named matches it whole. MEASURED_VERSIONS now holds 4 versions and Release::ALL 3 releases. Its judge set is ADDED_0_2_2_RC5 (agent-team, tool-agent-team, deepseek-account -> @deepseek-ai/dsh-deepseek-account) and REMOVED_0_2_2_RC5 (deepseek-account -> ...-platform), applied over 0.2.2-rc.1's set by a recursive arm in composition::measured. With brokkr-hands that is 102 rows. The variant is V0_2_2Rc5 rather than V0_2_2_RC5 because I expect rustc's non_camel_case_types lint, under -D warnings, to reject an underscore before a cased letter. I did not compile V0_2_2_RC5 to check.
- R2: V0_2_2_RC5_PINNED is the ten common rows, sandbox-policy, tool-executor-ptc, then tool-agent-team. The private const TEAM_TOOL_ROW holds that row's name. agent-team stays as composed, and the record says why.
- R3: the 0.2.1 and rc.1 arms are unchanged. Their overlay bytes and sets are unchanged, and the existing byte tests pass. One text did change: the version refusal (Refusal::Unmeasured) lists MEASURED_VERSIONS, so it now also names 0.2.2-rc.5. R1 requires that, and I updated the tail in only_a_measured_release_is_served_the_hands_rows to match. The composition refusal texts are unchanged.
- R4: a new section in docs/evidence/adapters/dsh-hands-0-2-2.md covers provenance (every live figure is the controller's), install and home, the composition diff, both tool lists, the sandbox rows, both digests and the offline bindings. Step 4 of the procedure names the rc.5 pin. Pending keeps its old items and adds rc.5-specific ones: a tool list and digest measured under the rc.5 overlay itself, a live workspace call, macOS, and the review-seat qualification.
- R5: #1056's F1 and F2 were not in my way, so I left them.

Tests: the five new tests are in dsh_hands/tests/releases.rs, a child of tests.rs, because tests.rs was at 1944 of its 2,000 lines. In tests.rs I factored the dump fixture into one dump_of(release, rows), so the rc.5 fixture adds no clone. tests.rs is now 1942 lines.
- a_0_2_2_rc5_tree_is_admitted
- a_0_2_2_rc5_row_is_refused_under_another_release
- a_0_2_2_rc5_tree_with_the_team_tool_enabled_is_refused
- only_0_2_2_rc5_whole_is_the_new_release: rc.2, rc.3, rc.4, 0.2.2 and rc.50 refuse, and the exact text names all four versions.
- the_0_2_2_rc5_overlay_is_pinned: the bytes, plus the bounded reader refusing either side.
Before this change the variant and tables did not exist, so the new tests could not compile, and the version text did not name rc.5.

Removal controls, both observed failing and then restored (recorded in the commit message):
- (i) Dropping the tool-agent-team pin failed a_0_2_2_rc5_tree_with_the_team_tool_enabled_is_refused (left None, right Some(Enabled{tool-agent-team})), plus the admitted and overlay-pinned tests.
- (ii) Admitting ADDED_0_2_2_RC5 into the V0_2_2 judge failed a_0_2_2_rc5_row_is_refused_under_another_release (left None, right Some(Unmeasured{agent-team, 0.2.2-rc.1})).

Gates run here:
- cargo fmt --check: clean.
- clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -D warnings: clean.
- adapters::dsh_hands: 103 passed.
- adapters::: 676 passed.
- brokkr-cli doc_truth:: and layering::test_targets: 38 passed.
- typos --hidden: clean.
- git diff --check: clean.
- ratchet files, clones and api: all hold.
- compile --bundle recipes/self: policy sweep 0 unruled.
- git status --short: empty.

Not verified:
- ratchet crap: refused with 'no LCOV at target/coverage/lcov.info'. That result and the exact-coverage gate belong to the host or CI. Every new production arm has a test.
- cargo test --workspace: did not finish within timeout 590 (exit 143), not retried.

The seat never set TMPDIR because the sandbox refuses env prefixes, so the tests used the default TMPDIR, which I believe is outside the worktree. git status shows nothing untracked.

Public API: no change; the api ratchet holds. No journal was opened outside a test temporary directory.
